_quarry.description: Three-canticle vernacular poem (Inferno, Purgatorio, Paradiso) composed by the exiled Florentine Dante between roughly 1308 and his death in 1321. Cast as a first-person journey through hell, purgatory, and heaven guided by Virgil and then Beatrice, the poem fused scholastic theology, Aristotelian cosmology, and personal political grievance — and in writing it in vernacular Tuscan rather than Latin, it helped establish that dialect as the prestige form of literary Italian.
